behavior_constraints: MERGE <key> <operand> appends operand to the key's value as a comma-separated list and outputs 'OK <seqnum>'
If key does not exist or was deleted, MERGE makes the operand the sole value
Multiple MERGEs stack: MERGE k a; MERGE k b; MERGE k c => GET k returns 'a,b,c'
PUT k x; MERGE k y; MERGE k z => GET k returns 'x,y,z'
MERGE entries use op_type 4 in WAL and SSTable records, storing the operand in the value field

Read path (GET, SCAN, snapshot reads, transaction reads) collects all MERGE entries for a key back to the most recent PUT or DELETE (or start of history) and folds them left-to-right with comma joining
TX_MERGE <tx_id> <key> <operand> and BATCH MERGE <key> <operand> behave identically to MERGE
During compaction, a run of MERGE entries for the same key collapses into a single entry only if no open snapshot needs the intermediate states
A run of MERGEs with no preceding PUT compacts into a single PUT whose value is the folded comma-joined result
STATS reports merge_operations = total number of uncompacted MERGE entries across the memtable and all SSTables
affected_prior: PointEntry / AllEntries / EntriesInRange (memtable must expose merge entries for folding)

entities.summary: This round adds a MERGE operator (op_type 4) that accumulates comma-separated operands across WAL, memtable, SSTables, snapshots, and transactions, with read-path left-to-right folding and compaction-time collapse of MERGE runs when no snapshot needs intermediates.

instruction_head: Add a merge operator. New command: `MERGE <key> <operand>` — appends the operand to the key's value as a comma-separated list. If the key already has a value from a previous PUT or MERGE, the new operand is appended with a comma separator. If the key doesn't exist or was deleted, the operand becomes the sole value. Multiple MERGEs stack: `MERGE k a`, `MERGE k b`, `MERGE k c` then `GET k` returns `a,b,c`. If a PUT preceded them — `PUT k x`, `MERGE k y`, `MERGE k z` — GET returns `x,y,z`. Output o
